stem: A 70-year-old woman has painful swallowing and burning behind the breastbone that began 3 weeks after she started a weekly tablet for osteoporosis. She takes it with a sip of water just before lying back down in bed. Endoscopy shows several erosions in the lower esophagus.
oneliner: 70F + new weekly tablet for osteoporosis + taken with a sip of water, then lies down + 3 wk later odynophagia + lower esophageal erosions → which drug?
ask: Which medication most likely caused this?

whyNot.A: **SERM**: risk is clots and hot flashes, not esophageal injury
whyNot.E: **Injection every 6 months**: no pill to stick in the esophagus

why: **Weekly osteoporosis tablet + little water + lying down → esophageal erosions** = pill esophagitis from a **bisphosphonate**. Take it upright with a full glass of water.

drug.name: Alendronate
drug.how: Binds bone hydroxyapatite and makes osteoclasts undergo apoptosis
drug.use: Osteoporosis, Paget disease, hypercalcemia of malignancy (IV forms)
drug.watch: Pill esophagitis, osteonecrosis of the jaw, atypical femur fractures

stem: A 58-year-old man with recurrent gout and a low 24-hour urinary uric acid excretion starts probenecid. Three weeks later he has sudden colicky left flank pain with hematuria. A plain abdominal film shows no stone shadow. He has no fever or rash, his creatinine and potassium are normal, and his urine volume is unchanged. He drinks little water.
oneliner: 58M + recurrent gout, low urinary uric acid + probenecid started + 3 wk later colicky flank pain, hematuria + no stone on plain film + normal creatinine and K → which drug effect?
ask: Which of the following drug effects most likely explains these symptoms?

options.A: Bladder mucosal injury from a toxic metabolite
options.B: Immune-mediated injury of the renal interstitium
options.C: Loss of collecting duct responsiveness to ADH

whyNot.A: Seen with **cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide** (acrolein); he takes neither, and his pain is **flank colic**
whyNot.B: Interstitial nephritis brings **fever, rash and rising creatinine**; he has **none**
whyNot.C: Causes **polyuria and dilute urine**; his **urine volume is unchanged**
whyNot.D: Would raise **potassium**, which is **normal**, and does not cause colic

answer: Uric acid stone from increased urinary uric acid
why: **Probenecid blocks urate reabsorption in the proximal tubule**, so more uric acid enters the urine. In a man who drinks little, that uric acid can precipitate as a **radiolucent uric acid stone** (colic, hematuria, nothing on plain film). Fluids and urine alkalinization reduce the risk.

drug.name: Probenecid
drug.how: Inhibits urate reabsorption (URAT1) and organic anion secretion in the proximal tubule, so more urate is excreted
drug.use: Gout from urate underexcretion; prolongs penicillin levels
drug.watch: Uric acid stones, initial gout flare, GI upset, rash; not for acute attacks or uric acid overproducers; aspirin blunts its effect

idea.rule: Uricosuric drugs move uric acid into the urine, so they can make uric acid stones.
also: Avoid uricosurics in uric acid overproducers and in stone formers; use allopurinol
Keep patients hydrated and alkalinize the urine when starting a uricosuric
Allopurinol lowers production and does not raise urinary uric acid
Aspirin in low doses blunts the uricosuric effect
